description: Find businesses in the directory by what they do (query, category: a group or a place category), where (near, country), the language they speak, whether they are open now, their attributes (list_attributes), price band, what their doors take and how they are paid (accepts: kinds, and ways to pay such as card, apple_pay, paypal or x402; each result's accepts.pay_with says whether the business declared each or it was only seen, on its site or in its shop platform's standard profile, and where), whether a door answers asks or quotes (requestable), the type of door, their readiness level, whether they have an inbox, and whether they are members, registered or found. Results come in the directory's published order, which nobody can pay to change; every filter only leaves businesses out. This server takes no orders or payments and books nothing itself: request_booking asks a business's own inbox for a time, and the business confirms it there. Each result lists the business's own doors. A business this network found on its own website is marked as found, with the date it was checked; a local one is listed once its site is matched to its entry on public maps or in a business register, or its owner proves the site is theirs. Software, API and AI companies (category software-ai) are kept apart: they come only when category names that group or one of its categories, query names their kind, or every word of query is in one's name. Pages of up to 20; pass next_cursor as cursor for more.

accepts.description: What its live doors take and what it accepts as payment, all of them: ask, quote, book, order, pay, or a payment from list_attributes like card or pix. This only leaves businesses out.

attributes.description: Keys from list_attributes, like "delivery" or "walk_ins", or key=value for one with values; every one must hold. This only leaves businesses out.

category.description: A slug from list_categories, like hair-beauty, or a place category id like hair_salon, with every category below it. Its label or a synonym works too. Under rules before version 7 any other word matches the tags businesses gave themselves; from version 7 it is an error that names up to 5 categories to try.

country.description: A country code like PT or BR: a business located there, serving it or shipping there. This only leaves businesses out.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous answer, for the next page of the same search.

door_type.description: A live door of any of these types: inbox, mcp, a2a, openapi, api, ucp, acp, nlweb, other, "platform" for any platform, or platform:<name>. This only leaves businesses out.

has_inbox.description: true: with an inbox door; false: without one. This only leaves businesses out.

item_type.description: Only businesses whose inbox takes this.

language.description: Only businesses that speak this language, as a tag like pt or en; pt also finds pt-br.

level.description: At this readiness level or above: askable (an AI can ask), bookable (a door takes bookings), orderable (a door takes orders), payable. bookable and orderable are one rung, and each asks for what the doors take. Nothing below askable is listed yet. This only leaves businesses out.

limit.description: How many to return: 10 when left out.

near.description: Only businesses within radius_km of this point, each with its distance.

radius_km.description: How far from the point, in kilometres: 10 when left out.

open_now.description: true: only businesses open right now by the hours they published. One that published no hours is left out.

order.description: rank: the published order (the default); nearest: by distance, and it needs near.

price_band.description: 1 (cheapest) to 4, as "2" or a range "1-2". This only leaves businesses out.

query.description: A few words about what the business does or where, like "florist" or "coffee singapore". Every word must match its name, town, description, categories, tags or services, ignoring capitals and accents. Words like "open" or "near me" belong in open_now and near instead.

requestable.description: A live door that declared it answers this kind. This only leaves businesses out.

source.description: member (through its inbox), registered (by the business), found (by this network on the business's own website); any of them. This only leaves businesses out.

name: search_businesses

businesses.description: In the directory's published order: no one can pay to move in it.

pay_with.description: Each of pay with its evidence, in the vocabulary's order. Absent from a listing built before it.

label.description: Its English name: Apple Pay for apple_pay.

url.description: The page, file, profile, manifest or door the evidence is at.

via.description: Where the evidence is: registration, manifest, schema_org, ucp, acp, door, file or page today. A later network may add one: read a via you do not know as evidence of its src.

answering.description: Its inbox answered this network within the last day.

group.description: Its group: a slug of GET /v1/categories.

path.description: Ancestor ids of the primary, root first, the primary last.

domain.description: The business's own domain, where its inbox is.

checked.description: A member's inbox door, on its detail: what the network's own reads last found in the past 24 hours (§4.8). answered; failing; could_not_check, the door refused the read (403, 429, a challenge page), so the business's signed ping alone says it answers. Absent when the network made no read.

level.description: What this door alone reaches, from the network's own probe.

protocol.description: The protocol it speaks, for type "other" only.

src.description: declared: the business said so; seen: read from the door's own tools.

status.description: failing: 3 failures in 7 days; it counts for nothing until it works.

about_url.description: The network's page for businesses: why it is here, and how to correct it or opt out.

note.description: "found on its own website · not a member · checked <YYYY-MM-DD>"

has_inbox.description: It has an inbox door: ours or any compatible inbox.

hours_today.description: Today's hours in its own time zone, like "09:00–13:00, 14:00–19:00", or "closed today"; null when it published none.

human_contact_only.description: It publishes only human channels; never served while nothing below askable is listed.

inbox.description: The business's own inbox, where it takes bookings, orders and questions; this server takes no orders or payments and books nothing itself. Present whenever has_inbox is true or absent.

mcp.description: Where an assistant books, orders or asks.

level.description: The highest level of its live doors (§4.9).

listing_url.description: Its full listing on this network (GET /v1/businesses/{domain}).

open_now.description: Open at the moment of the answer by the hours it published, in its own time zone; null when it published none.

place.description: For entries that are not members; a member keeps city, country and address.

ships_to.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, or ["*"] for anywhere.

requestable.description: The kinds a live door declared it answers; never from what the crawler saw alone.

services.description: Names and how each is taken; prices, durations and free times are at its inbox.

source.description: member: through its inbox; registered: by the business, with a proof; found: by the network's crawler.

standing.description: From the last nightly count of the promises it kept; absent while the directory's order is neutral.

broken.description: From rules version 8: the broken outcomes the night scored.

in_words.description: The tier in one plain sentence, or a self-reported record's counts; never a mark against the business.

kept.description: From rules version 8: the kept outcomes the night scored.

open.description: From rules version 8: its v2 promises still open.

ranked.description: Its record puts it before the daily shuffle.

self_reported.description: From rules version 8: its record rests on its own word (less than a fifth of it kept outcomes a verified acknowledgement backs), so it is not ranked and has no score; in_words says its counts.

verified_kept_share.description: From rules version 8, when not self_reported: the share of its record that is kept outcomes a verified acknowledgement backs (0.2 or more).

verified_share.description: From rules version 8, when not self_reported: the share of its record that is verified evidence.

tags.description: Other words the business gave for what it does.

takes.description: What its inbox takes: booking, order, quote_request, message, refund.

track_record.description: A member's track record, from the same nightly count as its standing and shown under the same rules: the promises it kept and broke, and when. From rules version 8, one that rests on the business's own word is self_reported: its counts, with no score and no count of customers. Only what its state can say is present; a business that is not a member has none.

as_of.description: The nightly count it is from (00:00 UTC).

broken.description: shown: closed as not kept by the business or by a customer's report that stands, left open 9 days past due, or a refund paid late.

closed.description: gathering and shown: kept plus broken.

confirmable.description: shown: whether this network can verify any acknowledgement yet (a recognised platform's agent key, or an established person's).

confirmed.description: shown: how many of the closed are kept outcomes a verified acknowledgement backs, confirmed by the customer's side (a customer's report is not a confirmation); the rest are the business's own word.

customers.description: gathering and shown, unless self_reported: the distinct customers the closed promises came from, as its receipts name them (the customer's mailbox when known, else, before rules version 8, the receipt's sub; from rules version 8 a sub that names no person is never a customer, and every receipt at a business that names nobody is one anonymous customer). Not reputation.customers, which counts only customers this network can tell apart.

from.description: shown: the earliest day of the evidence counted, at 00:00 UTC (a day, never the moment of a promise).

held_until.description: held: the night its record is counted from.

in_words.description: The record in one or two plain sentences, with how many of its closed promises the customer's side confirmed; the rest are the business's own word.

open.description: shown, from rules version 8: its v2 promises still open (reputation.open).

refunds_late.description: shown, of broken: refunds paid late (refund.late).

self_reported.description: gathering and shown, from rules version 8: the record rests on the business's own word (less than a fifth of it is kept outcomes a verified acknowledgement backs, as its reputation's self_reported), so it has no customers, and its threshold none.

state.description: held: a new member's 30 days after it joins, when nothing is counted; none: no receipts yet; pending: receipts the next nightly count reaches; gathering: fewer closed promises, or customers, than threshold; shown: the record.

threshold.description: What a record shows from: closed promises, from customers distinct customers; a self_reported record is not asked for customers, and has none here.

to.description: shown: the latest day of the evidence counted, at 00:00 UTC (a day, never the moment of a promise).

unclosed.description: shown, of broken: left open 9 days past due (promise.unclosed).

why.description: Why it is in this place of the list, in plain words.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as cursor for the next page; null on the last.

report.description: Report how each use of a door went, done or not: see the guide.

guide.description: How to report, for an agent: <network>/report.md.

reward.description: What the agent gets for reporting, in one sentence.

tool.description: The MCP tool that takes door reports: report_door.

rules.description: The rules that ordered these businesses (GET /v1/ranking?version=N).
